description: Spring 技术知识库 RAG 评测集，100 条人工标注样本（IC-6 v1.0）

samples.query: What is Inversion of Control (IoC) in Spring?
expected_answer_points: IoC container manages object creation and lifecycle
Dependencies are injected externally not instantiated internally
Reduces coupling between classes
ApplicationContext is the primary IoC container

samples.query: What is the difference between ApplicationContext and BeanFactory?
expected_answer_points: BeanFactory is the basic container with lazy initialization
ApplicationContext extends BeanFactory with eager bean initialization
ApplicationContext adds event propagation, i18n, and AOP integration
Prefer ApplicationContext in most Spring Boot applications

samples.query: What is the Spring Bean lifecycle from creation to destruction?
expected_answer_points: Instantiation via constructor
Dependency injection of properties
@PostConstruct or init-method callback
Bean ready for use
@PreDestroy or destroy-method on context close

samples.query: How does Spring AOP proxy creation work?
expected_answer_points: AOP creates proxies that wrap target beans
JDK dynamic proxy used when target implements interface
CGLIB subclass proxy used for concrete classes
Advice types: Before, After, Around, AfterReturning, AfterThrowing

samples.query: What are Spring stereotype annotations and their differences?
expected_answer_points: @Component is the generic stereotype
@Service semantically marks service layer
@Repository adds persistence exception translation
@Controller marks MVC controllers
All enable component scanning

samples.query: How does Spring MVC DispatcherServlet process requests?
expected_answer_points: DispatcherServlet implements Front Controller pattern
HandlerMapping finds the matching handler
HandlerAdapter invokes the handler method
ViewResolver resolves the logical view name
ModelAndView returned or @ResponseBody serialized

samples.query: What is Spring Boot AutoConfiguration and how is it enabled?
expected_answer_points: @SpringBootApplication enables auto-configuration scanning
Auto-configurations are @ConditionalOnClass/@ConditionalOnMissingBean
Boot 3.x: defined in META-INF/spring/org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.AutoConfiguration.imports
Boot 4.x: package paths relocated from o.s.boot.autoconfigure to o.s.boot.<module>.autoconfigure
samples.notes: Boot 4 relocated all autoconfigure packages — critical version-sensitive fact

samples.query: How do Spring Boot profiles work for environment-specific configuration?
expected_answer_points: @Profile annotation activates beans for specific profiles
spring.profiles.active property activates profiles
application-{profile}.yml files loaded for active profiles
Multiple profiles can be active simultaneously

samples.query: What is Spring Data JPA Repository and how does it simplify data access?
expected_answer_points: Repository interface eliminates boilerplate DAO code
JpaRepository provides full CRUD + paging + sorting
Derived query methods from method names (findByEmail)
Custom @Query for complex queries

samples.query: What is @Transactional and how does transaction propagation work?
expected_answer_points: @Transactional applies declarative transaction management via AOP proxy
REQUIRED propagation joins existing transaction or creates new
REQUIRES_NEW suspends current and starts independent transaction
readOnly=true hint allows optimizations for read queries

samples.query: What is the Spring Security filter chain architecture?
expected_answer_points: SecurityFilterChain is a @Bean in Spring Security 6 (replaces WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter)
Ordered servlet filters intercept every request
UsernamePasswordAuthenticationFilter handles form login
BasicAuthenticationFilter handles HTTP Basic
ExceptionTranslationFilter translates security exceptions

samples.query: What is CSRF protection and when should you disable it?
expected_answer_points: CSRF tokens prevent cross-site request forgery attacks
Spring Security adds CsrfFilter by default
Synchronizer Token Pattern embeds token in forms
Disable CSRF for stateless REST APIs using JWT/OAuth2

samples.query: How does the Spring Cache abstraction work?
expected_answer_points: @Cacheable caches method return value on first call
@CacheEvict removes entries from cache
@CachePut always updates cache without skipping method
Multiple backends via CacheManager (Redis, EhCache, Caffeine)

samples.query: What are Spring Boot Actuator endpoints and how do you secure them?
expected_answer_points: Actuator exposes operational endpoints (/health, /metrics, /info)
management.endpoints.web.exposure.include configures exposed endpoints
Secure with Spring Security or management.server.port isolation
Micrometer integration for metrics collection

samples.query: What is @ConfigurationProperties and how does type-safe binding work?
expected_answer_points: @ConfigurationProperties binds configuration hierarchies to POJOs
Relaxed binding (camelCase = kebab-case = UPPER_CASE)
@EnableConfigurationProperties or @ConfigurationPropertiesScan to register
Supports @Validated with Jakarta Bean Validation

samples.query: How does the Spring Event system work?
expected_answer_points: ApplicationEventPublisher.publishEvent() publishes events
@EventListener listens to typed events (Spring 4.2+)
@TransactionalEventListener binds to transaction phase
Events are synchronous by default; @Async for async handling

samples.query: What is Spring Expression Language (SpEL) and where is it used?
expected_answer_points: SpEL evaluates expressions at runtime using #{...} syntax
Used in @Value for dynamic property resolution
@PreAuthorize/@PostAuthorize for security expressions
@Cacheable key expressions, @Scheduled cron expressions

samples.query: What is RestClient and how does it differ from RestTemplate?
expected_answer_points: RestClient introduced in Spring 6.1 as synchronous replacement for RestTemplate
Fluent builder API: RestClient.builder().baseUrl().build()
RestTemplate is in maintenance mode since Spring 5.0
Both synchronous blocking; WebClient is the reactive option

samples.query: What is Spring Modulith and what problem does it solve?
expected_answer_points: Spring Modulith enforces modular monolith boundaries at build/test time
@ApplicationModule defines a module with allowed dependencies
internal package is inaccessible from other modules
Event-based inter-module communication via event_publication table

samples.query: What is Spring AI and what AI capabilities does it provide?
expected_answer_points: Spring AI 2.x is compatible with Spring Boot 4.x (1.x requires Boot 3.x)
ChatClient API for LLM conversations with streaming support
EmbeddingModel for text vectorization
VectorStore (including PgVectorStore) for RAG
Spring AI 2.x Anthropic integration uses official anthropic-java-core SDK

samples.query: How does @Async work in Spring and what are its requirements?
expected_answer_points: @EnableAsync activates async method execution
@Async marks methods to run in separate thread pool
Returns void, Future, or CompletableFuture
Cannot call @Async on same class (self-invocation bypasses proxy)

samples.query: What is Spring Batch and what is its Job/Step model?
expected_answer_points: Spring Batch 6.x is required for Spring Boot 4.x (5.x for Boot 3.x)
Job contains ordered Steps; each Step has ItemReader/Processor/Writer
Chunk-oriented processing reads/processes/writes in configurable chunks
JobRepository persists execution metadata for restartability
samples.notes: Batch 5.x on Boot 3.x, Batch 6.x on Boot 4.x

samples.query: What are virtual threads in Spring Boot and how do you enable them?
expected_answer_points: Virtual threads (Project Loom) available in Java 21
spring.threads.virtual.enabled=true in Boot 3.2+
Replaces ThreadPoolTaskExecutor with virtual thread factory
Enables high concurrency for blocking I/O (e.g., LLM calls) without tuning

samples.query: What is the difference between @Bean on @Configuration class vs @Component class?
expected_answer_points: Full @Configuration uses CGLIB subclass proxy for @Bean methods
Inter-@Bean method calls in full @Configuration return the same singleton
@Component with @Bean (lite mode) does NOT proxy — inter-bean calls create new instances
Use full @Configuration when @Bean methods call each other

samples.query: What changed in Spring Boot 4.x regarding autoconfigure package paths?
expected_answer_points: Boot 4 relocated ALL autoconfigure classes from o.s.boot.autoconfigure.<module> to o.s.boot.<module>.autoconfigure
Example: DataSourceAutoConfiguration moved to o.s.boot.jdbc.autoconfigure
All Boot 3 code that imports autoconfigure classes by name will fail to compile
Read META-INF/spring/org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.AutoConfiguration.imports for actual class names

samples.query: How do you configure multiple DataSources in Spring Boot?
expected_answer_points: Annotate primary DataSource with @Primary
Use @Qualifier to inject specific DataSource
Create separate @Bean TransactionManager for each DataSource
Configure separate EntityManagerFactory for each JPA DataSource

samples.query: How do you implement constructor injection in Spring?
expected_answer_points: Single constructor is auto-wired without @Autowired in Spring 4.3+
Use final fields for constructor-injected dependencies
@Autowired required for multiple constructors
Constructor injection makes dependencies explicit and enables immutability

samples.query: How do you implement global exception handling with @ControllerAdvice?
expected_answer_points: @RestControllerAdvice combines @ControllerAdvice + @ResponseBody
@ExceptionHandler methods catch specific exception types
ProblemDetail (RFC 7807) for structured error responses in Boot 3+
@ResponseStatus sets HTTP status code on exception class

samples.query: How do you configure @Transactional with custom rollback rules?
expected_answer_points: rollbackFor attribute specifies checked exceptions that trigger rollback
noRollbackFor excludes exceptions from rollback
RuntimeExceptions roll back by default
@Transactional(rollbackFor = {SomeCheckedException.class})

samples.query: How do you implement JWT authentication in Spring Security 6?
expected_answer_points: Define SecurityFilterChain @Bean with HttpSecurity lambda DSL
Use oauth2ResourceServer(OAuth2ResourceServerConfigurer::jwt)
Configure JwtDecoder bean from JWKS endpoint or secret
Custom OncePerRequestFilter for stateless JWT validation if not using OAuth2 auto-config

samples.query: How do you create a custom Spring Boot AutoConfiguration class?
expected_answer_points: Annotate class with @AutoConfiguration (not @Configuration)
@ConditionalOnClass / @ConditionalOnMissingBean for conditional activation
Register in META-INF/spring/org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.AutoConfiguration.imports
Boot 4: class package must use o.s.boot.<module>.autoconfigure convention
samples.notes: Boot 4 breaking change: Tracer bean not auto-configured

samples.query: How do you write JPQL queries with @Query in Spring Data JPA?
expected_answer_points: @Query on repository method with JPQL string
Use :paramName or ?1 positional parameters with @Param
@Modifying required for UPDATE/DELETE queries
nativeQuery=true for native SQL when JPQL is insufficient

samples.query: How do you implement pagination with Spring Data JPA?
expected_answer_points: Add Pageable parameter to repository method
Return Page<T> for total count or Slice<T> for streaming without count
PageRequest.of(page, size, Sort.by(...))
Use @PageableDefault for default pagination in controllers

samples.query: How do you configure Redis as the Spring Boot cache backend?
expected_answer_points: Add spring-boot-starter-data-redis dependency
Configure spring.data.redis.host and port
@EnableCaching activates cache infrastructure
RedisCacheManager auto-configured when Redis and Spring Cache are on classpath

samples.query: How do you integrate Testcontainers with @SpringBootTest in Boot 3.x?
expected_answer_points: Add testcontainers BOM and module dependencies
@Testcontainers on test class activates container management
@Container on static field starts container before Spring context
@ServiceConnection (Boot 3.1+) auto-configures datasource from container; @DynamicPropertySource for manual wiring

samples.query: How do you write a custom Spring MVC HandlerMethodArgumentResolver?
expected_answer_points: Implement HandlerMethodArgumentResolver interface
supportsParameter() returns true for handled parameter types
resolveArgument() extracts and returns the argument value
Register in WebMvcConfigurer.addArgumentResolvers()

samples.query: How do you configure distributed tracing in Spring Boot 4 with OpenTelemetry?
expected_answer_points: Boot 4 removed built-in Micrometer Tracing auto-configuration
Must manually create OpenTelemetrySdk and OtelTracer beans
Use micrometer-tracing-bridge-otel + opentelemetry-exporter-otlp dependencies
management.otlp.tracing.endpoint configures OTLP endpoint; avoid buildAndRegisterGlobal() in multi-context tests
samples.notes: Boot 4 breaking change: Tracer bean not auto-configured

samples.query: How do you implement method-level security with @PreAuthorize?
expected_answer_points: @EnableMethodSecurity on @Configuration class (replaces @EnableGlobalMethodSecurity in Security 6)
@PreAuthorize('hasRole("ADMIN")') on method
SpEL expressions access #argumentName
@PostAuthorize validates return value after method execution

samples.query: How do you configure CORS in a Spring MVC REST API?
expected_answer_points: @CrossOrigin on controller or method for simple cases
WebMvcConfigurer.addCorsMappings() for global configuration
CorsConfigurationSource @Bean needed when Spring Security is active
allowedOrigins, allowedMethods, allowedHeaders, allowCredentials

samples.query: How do you use Spring AI ChatClient to call an LLM with streaming?
expected_answer_points: Inject ChatClient.Builder and build per-call or keep singleton
.prompt().user(userMessage).call().content() for blocking
.prompt().user(userMessage).stream().content() returns Flux<String> for streaming
spring.ai.anthropic.api-key configures the API key via environment variable

samples.query: How do you set up a Spring Batch job with chunk-oriented processing in Spring Boot 4?
expected_answer_points: Use Spring Batch 6.x for Spring Boot 4.x
@EnableBatchProcessing optional in Boot 4 (auto-configuration handles it)
JobBuilder and StepBuilder for fluent job definition
chunk(chunkSize) sets read/process/write batch size

samples.query: How do you implement reliable event-driven communication between Spring Modulith modules?
expected_answer_points: ApplicationEventPublisher.publishEvent() within a @Transactional method writes to event_publication table
@ApplicationModuleListener on consumer method processes with retry support
Incomplete publications visible in /actuator/modulithEvents endpoint
Ensures at-least-once delivery even if consumer fails

samples.query: How do you tune HikariCP connection pool settings in Spring Boot?
expected_answer_points: spring.datasource.hikari.maximum-pool-size (default 10)
spring.datasource.hikari.minimum-idle prevents idle connections
spring.datasource.hikari.connection-timeout default 30s
Pool size guideline: (CPU cores * 2) + effective spindle count for DBs

samples.query: How do you use Spring Data Projections for read-only queries?
expected_answer_points: Interface-based projection: define interface with get-methods matching entity fields
DTO projection: @Value('#{target.field}') SpEL or constructor expression
Class-based projection for DTO with constructor
Limits SELECT columns — reduces data transfer

samples.query: How do you test a Spring MVC REST controller with MockMvc?
expected_answer_points: @WebMvcTest loads only web layer (no full context)
MockMvc.perform(get('/api/users')) with fluent API
andExpect(status().isOk()) verifies HTTP status
andExpect(jsonPath('$.name').value('Alice')) verifies JSON response

samples.query: How do you schedule recurring tasks with @Scheduled?
expected_answer_points: @EnableScheduling on @Configuration class enables scheduling
@Scheduled(cron = '0 0 * * * *') for cron expression
@Scheduled(fixedRate = 5000) for fixed-rate in milliseconds
spring.task.scheduling.pool.size for concurrent scheduled tasks

samples.query: How do you use Spring AI PgVectorStore for vector similarity search?
expected_answer_points: spring-ai-starter-vector-store-pgvector adds PgVectorStore auto-configuration
spring.ai.vectorstore.pgvector.initialize-schema=false lets Flyway manage schema
VectorStore.add(documents) stores embedded documents
VectorStore.similaritySearch(SearchRequest.builder().query().topK().build()) retrieves similar

samples.query: How do you implement a custom Spring Boot health indicator in Boot 4?
expected_answer_points: Implement HealthIndicator from org.springframework.boot.health.contributor (Boot 4 moved package)
Override health() method returning Health.up() or Health.down()
@Component registers the indicator
Health endpoint name derived from bean name minus 'HealthIndicator' suffix

samples.query: How do you configure Spring Boot for Kubernetes liveness and readiness probes?
expected_answer_points: management.health.probes.enabled=true activates Kubernetes probes
/actuator/health/liveness checks if app should be restarted
/actuator/health/readiness checks if app can receive traffic
Graceful shutdown with server.shutdown=graceful prevents traffic during termination

samples.query: How do you enforce Spring Modulith module boundaries in tests?
expected_answer_points: Create ModularityTests class calling ApplicationModules.of(App.class).verify()
@ApplicationModule(allowedDependencies={'moduleB'}) restricts inter-module imports
internal package classes inaccessible from other modules
ModularityTests runs at build time without Spring context startup

samples.query: What are the differences between field injection, setter injection, and constructor injection?
expected_answer_points: Constructor injection recommended: immutable, testable without Spring
Field injection hides dependencies and complicates testing
Setter injection for optional or reconfigurable dependencies
Spring 4.3+ auto-wires single constructors without @Autowired

samples.query: What changed in Spring Security configuration from version 5 to version 6?
expected_answer_points: WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter removed — use SecurityFilterChain @Bean instead
Lambda DSL required in Security 6 (no method chaining)
@EnableWebSecurity no longer needed explicitly in Boot apps
authorizeHttpRequests() replaces authorizeRequests()

samples.query: What is the javax.* to jakarta.* migration required by Spring 6?
expected_answer_points: Spring 6 requires Jakarta EE 9+ — all javax.* packages become jakarta.*
javax.persistence.Entity → jakarta.persistence.Entity
javax.validation.constraints → jakarta.validation.constraints
javax.servlet → jakarta.servlet — affects web components

samples.query: When should you use RestClient vs WebClient vs RestTemplate?
expected_answer_points: RestTemplate is in maintenance mode — not recommended for new code
RestClient (Spring 6.1) is the synchronous blocking replacement with fluent API
WebClient is for reactive/non-blocking use cases
Use RestClient in Spring MVC apps, WebClient in Spring WebFlux apps

samples.query: What are the differences between @SpringBootTest, @WebMvcTest, and @DataJpaTest?
expected_answer_points: @SpringBootTest loads full ApplicationContext — slowest but most comprehensive
@WebMvcTest loads only web layer — fast for controller tests, needs @MockBean for services
@DataJpaTest loads only JPA/Hibernate layer with in-memory DB by default
Slice tests significantly faster than full context tests

samples.query: What are the differences between JPQL, Criteria API, and QueryDSL in Spring Data?
expected_answer_points: JPQL is string-based, prone to runtime errors, readable for simple queries
Criteria API is type-safe at compile time but verbose
QueryDSL generates Q-classes from entities, most readable type-safe option
Spring Data supports all three via @Query, CriteriaBuilder, QuerydslPredicateExecutor

samples.query: What are the key differences between Spring Boot 2.x and Spring Boot 3.x?
expected_answer_points: Boot 3 requires Java 17 baseline (Boot 2 Java 8+)
javax.* packages replaced by jakarta.* throughout
Spring Security 6 with SecurityFilterChain replaces WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter
Native GraalVM image support; Boot 3.2+ adds virtual threads support

samples.query: What are the key differences between Spring Boot 3.x and Spring Boot 4.x?
expected_answer_points: Boot 4 requires Java 21 baseline (LTS)
All autoconfigure package paths relocated (o.s.boot.autoconfigure.<mod> → o.s.boot.<mod>.autoconfigure)
Spring AI 2.x required (1.x incompatible), Spring Batch 6.x required
MeterRegistryCustomizer moved to o.s.boot.micrometer.metrics.autoconfigure; Tracer not auto-configured

samples.query: What is the difference between REQUIRED and REQUIRES_NEW transaction propagation?
expected_answer_points: REQUIRED (default): joins existing transaction if present, creates new otherwise
REQUIRES_NEW: always creates a new independent transaction, suspends outer transaction
Use REQUIRES_NEW when inner transaction must commit/rollback independently
REQUIRES_NEW requires two database connections simultaneously

samples.query: When should you use @Value vs @ConfigurationProperties?
expected_answer_points: @Value for individual properties or SpEL expressions
@ConfigurationProperties for binding groups of properties to a POJO
@ConfigurationProperties supports validation and relaxed binding
@Value is simpler but less refactoring-safe for large config sets

samples.query: What is the difference between Spring MVC filters, interceptors, and AOP advice?
expected_answer_points: Servlet Filter operates before Spring context, wraps entire request/response
HandlerInterceptor is Spring MVC-aware, has access to handler and ModelAndView
AOP Advice operates at method level within Spring beans
Use Filter for cross-cutting request concerns, Interceptor for MVC-specific, AOP for service-layer

samples.query: When should you choose Spring WebFlux over Spring MVC?
expected_answer_points: WebFlux for high-concurrency non-blocking I/O (thousands of concurrent connections)
Spring MVC suitable for typical CRUD apps with moderate concurrency
Do not mix blocking code in WebFlux (kills scalability)
WebFlux uses Project Reactor Mono/Flux instead of plain objects

samples.query: What are the differences between Flyway and Liquibase for schema migration?
expected_answer_points: Flyway uses SQL or Java migration scripts with checksum validation
Liquibase uses XML/YAML/JSON changesets with rollback support
Both integrate with Spring Boot auto-configuration
Flyway simpler for SQL-first teams; Liquibase better for complex rollback needs

samples.query: What is the difference between JPA optimistic and pessimistic locking?
expected_answer_points: Optimistic locking uses @Version column checked at commit time — no DB lock held
Pessimistic locking uses SELECT FOR UPDATE — holds DB lock for transaction duration
Optimistic locking better for low-contention read-heavy scenarios
@Lock(LockModeType.PESSIMISTIC_WRITE) on repository method for pessimistic

samples.query: What are the differences between Spring AOP JDK proxy and CGLIB proxy?
expected_answer_points: JDK dynamic proxy requires target to implement interface, proxies through interface methods
CGLIB creates subclass of target class, works without interface
Spring uses CGLIB by default since 4.0 even for interface-bearing classes
Final classes/methods cannot be CGLIB-proxied

samples.query: What is the difference between Spring Data JPA and Spring Data JDBC?
expected_answer_points: Spring Data JPA uses Hibernate/ORM with lazy loading, caching, complex relationships
Spring Data JDBC is simpler: no lazy loading, no session cache, no ORM overhead
JDBC follows aggregate pattern — load complete aggregates at once
JDBC better performance predictability; JPA better for complex domain models

samples.query: How did Spring Security HttpSecurity configuration change from Security 5 to 6?
expected_answer_points: Security 5: chainable method calls (http.authorizeRequests().antMatchers().and().csrf())
Security 6: lambda DSL required (http.authorizeHttpRequests(auth -> ...).csrf(csrf -> ...))
Security 6: antMatchers() removed, use requestMatchers()
andHttpBasic() replaced by httpBasic(Customizer.withDefaults())

samples.query: When should you use @Cacheable, @CachePut, and @CacheEvict?
expected_answer_points: @Cacheable: cache-aside — returns cached value if present, stores result on miss
@CachePut: write-through — always executes method and updates cache
@CacheEvict: removes entry from cache on method execution
Combine @Caching to apply multiple cache annotations to one method

samples.query: What is the difference between @Configuration full mode and @Component lite mode for @Bean?
expected_answer_points: Full @Configuration: CGLIB subclass intercepts @Bean method calls — returns same singleton
Lite mode (@Component with @Bean): no CGLIB proxy — inter-bean method calls create new instances
proxyBeanMethods=false on @Configuration opts into lite mode for performance
Always use full @Configuration when @Bean methods call each other

samples.query: What are the differences between embedded Tomcat, Jetty, and Undertow in Spring Boot?
expected_answer_points: Tomcat is the default embedded server in spring-boot-starter-web
Jetty has smaller memory footprint; exclude Tomcat and add spring-boot-starter-jetty
Undertow is NIO-based, performant for non-blocking use cases
Switch servers by excluding spring-boot-starter-tomcat and adding desired starter

samples.query: What are the differences between @PostConstruct, InitializingBean, and @Bean(initMethod)?
expected_answer_points: @PostConstruct is JSR-250 (jakarta.annotation) — portable, preferred
InitializingBean.afterPropertiesSet() is Spring-specific coupling
@Bean(initMethod='init') for third-party classes you cannot annotate
All called after dependency injection; @PostConstruct before afterPropertiesSet()

samples.query: When should you use Spring Security form login vs HTTP Basic vs JWT?
expected_answer_points: Form login for browser-based applications with session cookies
HTTP Basic for simple machine-to-machine APIs (HTTPS required)
JWT for stateless REST APIs and SPAs — no server-side session
OAuth2 + JWT for federated identity and third-party integrations

samples.query: What is the difference between Micrometer and OpenTelemetry for Spring observability?
expected_answer_points: Micrometer is the metrics facade in Spring (analogous to SLF4J for logging)
OpenTelemetry provides distributed tracing plus metrics plus logs
micrometer-tracing-bridge-otel bridges Micrometer Tracing API to OTel backend
Spring AI uses OTel GenAI semantic conventions for LLM span attributes

samples.query: What changed in Spring Batch from version 4.x to 5.x to 6.x?
expected_answer_points: Batch 4.x: Spring Boot 2.x, Java 8+, javax.* annotations
Batch 5.x: Spring Boot 3.x, Java 17 baseline, jakarta.* annotations, @EnableBatchProcessing optional in Boot 3
Batch 6.x: Spring Boot 4.x, Java 21 baseline; incompatible with Boot 3
Always align Batch version with Spring Boot major version

samples.query: What is the difference between @EventListener and @ApplicationModuleListener in Spring Modulith?
expected_answer_points: @EventListener is standard Spring — not persisted, no retry on failure
@ApplicationModuleListener persists event to event_publication table before delivery
@ApplicationModuleListener auto-retries failed listeners for at-least-once delivery
Spring Modulith event system provides durability guarantees missing from @EventListener

samples.query: What are the best practices for Spring Boot externalized configuration?
expected_answer_points: Use @ConfigurationProperties over @Value for grouped config
Never store secrets in application.yml — use environment variables or secrets manager
spring.config.import=optional:configserver: for Config Server
Use spring.profiles.active for environment-specific overrides

samples.query: What are the best practices for Spring Security password encoding?
expected_answer_points: Always use BCryptPasswordEncoder or Argon2 — never plain text or MD5/SHA
BCrypt work factor 10-12 balances security and performance
DelegatingPasswordEncoder supports multiple encoders with {bcrypt} prefix for migration
PasswordEncoder.encode() on registration, matches() on authentication

samples.query: How do you prevent and fix the JPA N+1 query problem?
expected_answer_points: N+1 occurs when lazy collection is accessed per entity in a loop
Fix with JOIN FETCH in JPQL: 'SELECT u FROM User u JOIN FETCH u.orders'
@EntityGraph on repository method specifies fetch strategy
Enable Hibernate SQL logging to detect N+1: spring.jpa.show-sql=true

samples.query: What are the best practices for Spring Boot production configuration?
expected_answer_points: Enable graceful shutdown: server.shutdown=graceful
Configure actuator with security: management.server.port=8081 on internal network
Set JVM max heap appropriate for container memory limits
Externalize all credentials with SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL style env vars

samples.query: What are the best practices for designing Spring Data JPA repositories?
expected_answer_points: One repository per aggregate root — avoid spanning multiple entities
Use projections (interface or DTO) for read-only queries to limit SELECT columns
Separate read repositories from write repositories for CQRS-lite
@Transactional(readOnly=true) on query methods for read-only hint to Hibernate

samples.query: What are the best practices for Spring Boot REST API exception handling?
expected_answer_points: Use @RestControllerAdvice for centralized exception handling
Return ProblemDetail (RFC 7807) for machine-readable error responses (Boot 3+)
Map domain exceptions to HTTP status codes — never expose stack traces
Log server errors with correlation ID from OTel trace context

samples.query: What are the best practices for Spring transaction management?
expected_answer_points: Apply @Transactional at service layer, not controller or repository
@Transactional(readOnly=true) on all read-only service methods
Avoid catching exceptions inside @Transactional (prevents rollback)
Self-invocation bypasses @Transactional — inject self or restructure

samples.query: What are Spring Boot security hardening best practices?
expected_answer_points: Enable HSTS: http.headers(h -> h.httpStrictTransportSecurity(hsts -> hsts.includeSubDomains(true)))
Set Content-Security-Policy header to prevent XSS
Disable X-Frame-Options ALLOW for non-iframe apps
Use management.server.port for separate actuator network to restrict admin access

samples.query: What are the best practices for containerizing Spring Boot applications?
expected_answer_points: Use multi-stage Dockerfile: Maven/Gradle build stage + JRE runtime stage
Leverage Spring Boot layered JARs for optimal Docker layer caching
Set -Xmx to 75% of container memory limit
Non-root USER in Dockerfile; EXPOSE the application port

samples.query: What are the best practices for testing Spring Boot applications?
expected_answer_points: Use test pyramid: many unit tests, fewer slice tests, few full @SpringBootTest
Prefer Testcontainers over in-memory H2 for realistic DB testing
Use @WebMvcTest for controller tests with @MockBean for service dependencies
Avoid @SpringBootTest unless full context integration is needed

samples.query: What are the best practices for HikariCP connection pool tuning?
expected_answer_points: Set maximum-pool-size based on database thread count: (CPU_cores * 2) + disk spindles
idle-timeout evicts connections not used for 10 minutes by default
connection-timeout (30s default) should be less than network timeout
Monitor pool metrics via spring.datasource.hikari.pool-name and Micrometer

samples.query: What are the best practices for Spring Security in stateless REST APIs?
expected_answer_points: Disable CSRF (stateless — no cookies): csrf(csrf -> csrf.disable())
Configure CORS for SPA origin: CorsConfigurationSource @Bean
Use OAuth2 Resource Server for JWT validation: oauth2ResourceServer(oauth2 -> oauth2.jwt(...))
Rate limiting at gateway or via Resilience4j @RateLimiter

samples.query: What are the performance best practices for Spring AOP?
expected_answer_points: Narrow pointcut expressions to avoid scanning all methods
Prefer @Around only when you need both pre and post behavior — use @Before/@After when possible
AspectJ weave-time weaving faster than Spring proxy-based AOP at runtime
Avoid AOP on frequently-called fine-grained methods (per-call overhead)

samples.query: What are the best practices for Spring Boot observability with OpenTelemetry in Boot 4?
expected_answer_points: Boot 4 removes Tracer auto-config — manually wire OpenTelemetrySdk + OtelTracer
Do not call buildAndRegisterGlobal() in multi-context tests (causes conflict)
Include traceId/spanId in log pattern: %X{traceId}
For LLM calls follow OTel GenAI semantic conventions: gen_ai.system, gen_ai.usage.input_tokens
